Hi Marta — great to hear. We're excited to partner on the MVP. Attaching a short mutual action plan and an SDK snippets bundle to get your devs started (redwood-sdk-snippets.zip, mutual-action-plan.xlsx).

High-level plan we recommend:
- Week 1: SDK quickstart + auth (API keys or mTLS), basic generate call, and run smoke tests.
- Week 2: Endpoint migration shadowing (send mirrored traffic to Redwood for non-prod).
- Week 3: Cutover window + rollback playbook.

Quick auth note: for production we suggest customer-managed keys (KMS) + per-service tokens. We'll document the steps in the kickoff.

Proposed kickoff: Tue 2026-10-13 10:00 PT. Does that work for your team?

I'll also include a short technical note below with suggested retry/backoff defaults your engineers can try initially.

Suggested retry pattern (start conservative, tune later):
- Idempotent requests (embeddings, fetch metadata): retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff (base 200ms, factor 2), jitter 100-300ms.
- Non-idempotent generation calls: prefer client-side token streaming and server-side safe-fallthrough; use 429 handling + single retry after backoff.
- Timeouts: connection 2s, read/response 12s for short chats, 60s for longer generation windows.

I'll share sample code in a follow-up message.

— Marissa

Hey Marta — quick answers ahead of the kickoff tomorrow:

1) Starter tier throughput: for shadowing we recommend keeping mirrored traffic under ~10 RPM (requests per minute) per API key for generation endpoints to avoid hitting concurrency limits. If you expect bursts, we can enable a temporary burst policy for the shadow project during the 72-hour run.

2) 429 strategy: prefer client-side throttling + exponential backoff. Practical flow:
   - On 429: pause new requests for a backoff window (see David's snippet), retry up to N times.
   - If 429s continue at scale, reduce concurrency rather than increasing retries to avoid amplifying pressure on the service.
   - We'll also instrument a soft quota signal and can increase capacity on our side for the shadow project for a short period if you want to test higher throughput.

Operational playbook for the cutover (short):
- 48h before cutover: run full shadowing for 72h to collect metrics (latency, token counts, error rates).
- Cutover window (2-4 hours): progressive percentage routing (10/30/60/100) across 30–45 minute buckets, rollback to previous vendor if error rate > 2% or latency > 2x baseline.
- Post-cutover (24h): monitor token-level costs and error spikes; revert if SLOs are breached.

I'll have an operations runbook as a Google Doc after the kickoff. For the meeting, please share Carlos and Priya's calendar invites; I'll send a dial-in + short agenda.

— Vivek
